P1.evidence: No application or setter notes read back at any point — the prospect referenced his own form ("I think I put in my thing") and the rep did not pick it up. Three-part frame again: "go through where you're at at the moment, where you want to go. See if we can help you reach that gap. If you can, I'll take you through how? If not, perfectly fine." Agreement taken and the open question run. Credit where due outside the checklist: the rep opened by confirming the prospect was parked and had a clear 45 minutes, and offered to reschedule.

P2.evidence: The injury screen was run properly and pushed for completeness — "anything else that you feel, maybe your lower back, hamstrings... or is it mainly shoulders and upper back?" — and the rep correctly picked up the knee stiffness the prospect was dismissing. Diet was worked well including the home-versus-out distinction. But age, height, weight and occupation were all volunteered and none was asked, and the two most consequential omissions are unmissable: the prospect said the words "undiagnosed sleep apnea" and "my father did pass away, and as far as we can tell, it was from a heart attack" and "my grandparents both had diabetes", and no health-history or sleep question was asked at any point in the call. Training frequency was never established.

P3.evidence: The strongest phase in the batch. The why question was asked in the ICP's own frame — "there's so many people out there that are obese, don't really care, you're 33, you're 5'9", 240, there's so many people are okay with that... Why is that not enough for you?" — and it opened everything: the joints, the grandparents, the father-in-law. The rep then asked the best question of the batch: "you started to go back into training like a year ago, right? What was that why for you?", which produced the marriage crisis. The reflect-back was textbook and confirmed: "you want to focus on getting your energy in place and keeping it in place, having that longevity aspect, and also just getting your joints more freed up, and then the weight is going to be a byproduct" / "100%." Marked partial on P3g only because the father's death was received and immediately passed over.

P4.evidence: The need question was asked directly — "when you would start working with Trevor, what is the thing that you would really need?" — and the prospect named the gap cleanly himself: "It's more for the accountability side of it" and "I'm not good at making workouts right now... sometimes putting it together into a workout." But past attempts were never asked about. The carnivore diet, the six years out of the gym and the lapsed Olympic weightlifting with his wife all surfaced because he volunteered them, and none was followed with 'what happened' or 'why didn't it stick'. The self-reliance challenge was never put — which matters here, because he answered it himself in the negative twice ("I'm going to figure out a way whether or not I can do this or not").

P5.evidence: This phase collapsed and it cost the close. The two-year consequence question was never asked. The settle question was attempted three times and was incomprehensible each time — "Are you willing for the fact where you're not going to get better?" drew "What's that?", the rephrase drew "I'm not sure I'm following what you're saying", and the third attempt finally landed a partial answer. Worse, the answer it produced was the escape hatch: "if it didn't work here, I'd try somewhere else." That exact sentence came back at 00:50:49 as his reason not to decide — "if I don't do it here, I'm going to find somewhere else." The rep let it stand unchallenged both times. Line in the sand reduced to "Ready to make the differences there?" / "Yeah."

P6.evidence: Both commitment questions were asked and answered well — "when you have all of those three in place, can you think of any reason why you're not going to be able to be successful?" / "Not really, unless something was just catastrophic", followed by "do you feel like you're ready to, instead of taking those small steps, to actually take a big one?" / "I feel like, yes. Let's get there." But both came at 00:44:00, after the full presentation ran from 00:30:51 to 00:42:01. The script requires the yes before anything is presented. Had it been asked in the right order, the fact that a $6,000 decision was jointly held with a wife who had never heard of this would have surfaced before the pitch rather than three minutes after the price.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted but the prospect deferred pending a conversation with his wife, so payment and onboarding were never reachable. Noted separately as a process failure rather than a P11 check: the follow-up was not locked on the call — the rep was already eight minutes late for his next meeting and said "I will send you the invite for that sometime tomorrow", leaving the highest-intent prospect of the batch with no calendar hold.

objection_plays.detail: The best-run objection play in the batch, and still half the script. Ran: isolation to money ("outside of the investment... do you feel like, yeah, I do see myself doing this?"), her likely reaction ("what do you think her initial reaction is going to be just on the program itself?"), the thumbs-up test ("if she would say okay, you should go for it, would you actually go for it as well?" / "If she gave me the thumbs up, absolutely"), and the what-if-no question. Did not run: "is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain?", "is this genuinely needing her input — or asking permission to bet on yourself?", "this isn't a joint decision like buying a house — is that responsibility hers or yours?", and the deposit-with-refund fallback. The rep also volunteered the frame that legitimised the delay — "I don't want you to sleep on the couch anyway."

Trigger was clear and repeated ("a little more than I had in mind", "a bit of sticker shock", "the most I've ever spent on something fitness-wise", "there's other things that I think she'd probably rather spend money towards"). The rep isolated it and ran the future-worth check, which the prospect answered strongly in the affirmative. Then nothing: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no cards, no available credit, no investments, no "most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up". A payment plan was never mentioned even though the prospect's only stated blocker was the size of a single number and internal calls the same week confirm six-instalment plans and deposits are in active use. The prospect even handed the rep the price-as-commitment argument himself ("if it's just a hundred, you don't care") and it was never converted into a structure.

"Something I have to think about" and later "I'll just have to talk with her about it and really think more on it myself to be able to make a decision." Treated entirely as the spouse objection; no OA move ran. Nothing on "thinking isn't the problem, deciding is", nothing on "the way you've been approaching this brought you here" — which was available, since the prospect had spent forty minutes describing himself as a man who makes excuses.

Script gap, clinical. The prospect disclosed a shoulder injury actively aggravated by the modality being sold ("the kettlebells have definitely brought that out"), stated his own equipment was unsafe for him ("I feel like I could hurt myself more if I do it wrong"), and disclosed reconstructive wrist surgery, treated sleep apnea and a first-degree family history of fatal heart attack, all at a BMI around 35. There is no scripted screen for any of it. The rep answered the shoulder concern with a benefit claim — "you're not going to feel your shoulders that much, your upper back will get more straight" — which is the improvisation the playbook's own known_gaps section predicts.

notes: Best discovery of the batch by some distance — the 'why is that not enough for you' question and the follow-up into why he returned to the gym a year ago produced more usable material than any other call here, and the reflect-back was exemplary. Three things lost it, none of them about the ending: the consequence frame was so badly phrased the prospect twice said he could not follow it and answered with the exact escape line he later used to defer; the commitment check ran after the presentation instead of before, so a jointly-held $6,000 decision surfaced only after the price; and no payment plan was offered to a prospect whose sole objection was the size of one payment.
